Name: Performance of fiscal agents.
Title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to the performance of fiscal agents

History.Description: This Introduction was Introduced by Council
This Introduction was Referred to Comm by Council to the Committee on Children and Youth

Summary: This bill would require the Department of Youth and Community Development (DYCD) to submit an annual report detailing the performance of any fiscal agents they have contracted with to perform financial administration tasks on behalf of a community-based organization, including receiving, holding, disbursing, processing, and recording funds or payments. The bill would also require DYCD to establish a feedback mechanism for community-based organizations to submit feedback about any fiscal agents used.
Text:
Be it enacted by the Council as follows:


Section 1. Chapter 4 of title 21 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding a new section 21-416 to read as follows:
§ 21-416 Fiscal agent reporting. a. Definitions. For purposes of this section, the following terms have the following meanings:
Community-based organization. The term “community-based organization” means a non-profit organization contracted by the department to provide services to, or operate for the benefit of, a particular community.
Fiscal agent. The term “fiscal agent” means an entity contracted by the department to perform financial administration tasks on behalf of a community-based organization, including receiving, holding, disbursing, processing, and recording funds or payments.
b. Report. The department shall submit an annual report to the council detailing:
1. The number of grants managed by each fiscal agent;
2. Average times for processing invoices and contract actions;
3. The number and nature of complaints received from community-based organizations regarding each fiscal agent, and the number of such complaints resolved; and 
4. Performance metrics for evaluating fiscal agents including, but not limited to, timeliness standards for invoice processing and contract actions, responsiveness to community-based organization inquiries, and any additional indicators the department deems appropriate. 
c. Feedback. The department shall establish a mechanism through which community-based organizations may submit feedback or grievances regarding the performance of any fiscal agent. Actions the department may take to address substantiated concerns may include, but not be limited to:
1. Requesting corrective action from the fiscal agent;
2. Increasing departmental monitoring or oversight; 
3. Facilitating communication between the organization and the fiscal agent, requiring additional training for fiscal agent staff; or 
4. Where all other remedies have been exhausted, providing direct financial administration support by department staff in place of a fiscal agent, to the extent permitted by applicable procurement rules and existing contracts. 
§ 2. This local law takes effect 90 days after it becomes law.
